vectors.label: ASCII case
vectors.why: The trivial case every engineer believes they have handled.

vectors.label: Non-ASCII case
vectors.why: Only the non-ASCII character differs in case. SQLite NOCASE folds A-Z only, so this pair slips through.

codepointsA.name: LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E WITH ACUTE

codepointsB.name: LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE

vectors.label: Accent folding
vectors.why: MySQL utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci folds accents; utf8mb4_0900_as_cs does not.

codepointsA.name: LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE

vectors.label: Sharp s expansion
vectors.why: German sharp s casefolds to 'ss', changing the string length.

vectors.label: NFC vs NFD
vectors.why: macOS writes the decomposed form, Windows the composed form. Same pixels, different bytes.

codepointsA.name: LATIN SMALL LETTER E WITH ACUTE

vectors.label: Trailing space
vectors.why: MySQL PAD SPACE and SQLite RTRIM trim it; MySQL 0900 and SQLite BINARY do not.

vectors.label: Kelvin sign vs k
vectors.why: U+212A KELVIN SIGN lowercases to 'k' in Unicode-aware code but not in ASCII folding.

vectors.label: Ligature vs letters
vectors.why: U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI survives casefold; only NFKC decomposes it.

vectors.label: Dotted capital I
vectors.why: U+0130 casefolds to TWO code points, so a fixed-width hash assumption breaks.

codepointsA.name: LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE

vectors.label: Fullwidth A
vectors.why: U+FF21 is only folded by NFKC compatibility decomposition.

vectors.label: Combining mark in Arabic
vectors.why: U+1E25 ARABIC LETTER HA WITH DOT BELOW - an accent no ASCII rule notices.

codepointsB.name: LATIN SMALL LETTER H WITH DOT BELOW

vectors.label: Cyrillic a vs Latin a
vectors.why: U+0430 CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER A. No engine folds confusables - only UTS #39 does.

engines.label: SQLite BINARY (default)
engines.note: Byte-for-byte comparison. This is what you get if you write nothing.

engines.label: SQLite NOCASE
engines.note: Folds the 26 ASCII letters only. Non-ASCII case is untouched.

engines.label: SQLite RTRIM
engines.note: Strips trailing spaces before comparing. Combines with the default byte comparison.

engines.label: SQLite COLLATE NFC_FOLD (custom)
engines.note: Custom collation: NFC normalise, then casefold. Registered with create_collation().

engines.label: SQLite COLLATE NFKC_FOLD (custom)
engines.note: Custom collation: NFKC normalise, casefold, strip. The widest net.

engines.label: DuckDB (default)
engines.note: Exact comparison; DuckDB applies no case folding of its own.

engines.label: DuckDB NOCASE
engines.note: Case-insensitive collation. Accent behaviour differs from SQLite NOCASE.

engines.label: PostgreSQL (database default)
engines.note: Whatever the cluster was created with. In most managed services this is a C-family collation: byte exact.

engines.label: PostgreSQL COLLATE "C"
engines.note: Byte-order comparison. Deterministic, case sensitive, accent sensitive. [calibrated: caseSensitive=true, codePointOrder=true]

engines.label: PostgreSQL COLLATE "ucs_basic"
engines.note: Code-point order for text. Deterministic - no folding of any kind. [calibrated: caseSensitive=true, codePointOrder=true]

engines.label: PostgreSQL COLLATE "en_US.utf8"
engines.note: A glibc locale. If it is functional it sorts alphabetically ('a' before 'B'); equality stays case sensitive.

engines.label: PostgreSQL COLLATE "unicode" (ICU)
engines.note: ICU collation, still deterministic - tertiary differences such as case remain significant, but ordering is alphabetical. [calibrated: caseSensitive=true, codePointOrder=false]

engines.label: PostgreSQL nondeterministic ICU (primary strength)
engines.note: deterministic = false at primary strength: case- and accent-insensitive. This is PostgreSQL's answer to MySQL utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci.

claims.source: Stack Overflow, "How to make a case-insensitive unique column in SQLite" (answer score 300+, 2013)
claims.text: Declare the column COLLATE NOCASE and your uniqueness problem is solved.

claims.source: sqlite.org - Datatypes In SQLite, section 3.1 (Built-in Collating Sequences)
claims.text: NOCASE folds only the 26 upper case characters of ASCII to lower case before comparing.

claims.source: sqlite.org - Datatypes In SQLite, section 3.1 (BINARY is the default)
claims.text: BINARY is the default collation and compares strings byte for byte.

claims.source: Widespread practice - "just lowercase the email address before storing it"
claims.text: Lower-casing the address before insert removes case-driven duplicates.

claims.source: Widespread practice - toLowerCase() applied to the e-mail column in Node
claims.text: toLowerCase() before insert removes case-driven duplicates.

claims.source: dev.mysql.com - Character Sets, Collations, Unicode, section 10.9.1 (The _bin Collations for Unicode)
claims.text: Older MySQL collations such as utf8mb4_general_ci are PAD SPACE: 'a' and 'a ' compare equal inside a unique index.

claims.source: dev.mysql.com - Unicode Character Sets, 10.9.2 The utf8mb4 Collations (0900 family are NO PAD)
claims.text: The utf8mb4_0900_* family introduced in MySQL 8.0 is NO PAD, so 'a' and 'a ' stay two distinct rows in the very same table definition.
utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci is case- and accent-insensitive, so Jose and José collide.

claims.source: postgresql.org - CREATE COLLATION, nondeterministic subtransactions note (deterministic = false)
claims.text: A nondeterministic ICU collation compares at the primary level only, so an accent does not prevent equality.
normalize(text, NFC) canonicalises both forms before an expression index compares them.

claims.source: Unicode UTS #39 - Unicode Security Mechanisms, confusable detection
claims.text: Collation and normalisation do not fold confusable characters. Cyrillic a and Latin a stay distinct in every engine; only confusable detection catches them.

claims.source: Unicode UAX #15 - Unicode Normalization Forms, section 6 Compatibility Decomposition
claims.text: NFKC folds the compatibility decompositions, so fullwidth A becomes plain A.

claims.source: Unicode data - simple lowercase mapping vs full case folding (Python str.lower)
claims.text: str.lower() performs a simple lowercase mapping and leaves U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI untouched, so it does not merge this pair.

claims.source: Unicode CaseFolding.txt, status F (full) mappings, used by Python str.casefold
claims.text: str.casefold() applies the full case-folding mapping, which expands U+FB01 to the two ASCII letters 'fi'.
